summary: prosocks installs a hardcoded-panel SOCKS5 proxy backdoor with Windows boot persistence
details: setup.py's PostInstallCommand runs at pip install time and (a) spawns a detached background process that binds a SOCKS5 proxy on 0.0.0.0:9050 on the installer's host and (b) writes a.bat launcher into the Windows Start Menu Startup folder so the proxy re-launches on every login. The launched module (prosocks) fetches the host's public IP via api.ipify.org and POSTs an agent_id, proxy_port, and generated SOCKS5 password to the hardcoded control panel https://kalnetz.store/api/register, followed by periodic heartbeat and bandwidth reports. All outbound calls to the panel and to the IP-lookup service are made with TLS verification disabled (verify=False). The net effect of pip installing this package is that the installer's machine is turned into an attacker-controlled, world-reachable SOCKS5 relay whose credentials and public IP are handed to the operator of kalnetz.store, with automatic reconnection across reboots on Windows.
